what: Fianna the sketch-mage: a slim young woman of about eighteen, painted seriously with realistic proportions, a small head, about seven and a half heads tall, long legs. Her head is bare. Her hair is long, slightly wavy and flowing, very dark brown, almost black, falling past her shoulders and lifting and streaming out to one side in the wind of her magic. Her face is turned toward the viewer, light-skinned and brightly lit from the front, the palest and clearest thing on her, framed by the dark hair: two dark eyes and two dark eyebrows plainly marked, a small nose, closed lips, an intent, delighted look.
colours: a deep cool violet-purple robe, the purple of wild violets, with a thin gold border, a dark brown leather belt and boots, a big sketchbook with a dark brown leather cover and cream-white pages, a long white feather quill, a creature of glowing pale lilac-lavender light, plainly light purple, outlined in bold black ink lines, wisps of the same lilac-lavender light, light skin, very dark brown hair that is almost black.
wears: She wears a long, loose, deep cool violet-purple robe, the purple of wild violets, with long wide sleeves and a high round neck, reaching to her ankles, trimmed with a thin gold border at the hem and cuffs, closed at the waist with a dark brown leather belt; dark brown boots show beneath. Her head is bare, with nothing on it but her flowing dark hair.
holds: She holds exactly two things. In her left hand, held out to the left of her body at chest height, at arm's length and clear of her body, is one big open sketchbook, the size of a large book, its cream pages facing up and toward the viewer. In her right hand she holds exactly one long white feather quill, as long as her forearm, its tip touching the page, drawing. Leaping out of the open pages toward the left is a phantom wolf she has just sketched, as big as her upper body, seen from the side: a wolf's long narrow muzzle with open jaws, two tall pointed ears standing straight up, a deep chest and two front legs stretched out ahead of it in a running leap. Every edge of it is outlined in a thick, bold black ink line, like a bold pen drawing, and a few thick black ink strokes mark its eye, its mouth and the lie of its fur; between the lines it is filled with glowing pale lilac-lavender light, plainly light purple, the colour of lavender flowers mixed with white. Its back half is not drawn yet: there it dissolves into three or four broad swirling wisps of the same lilac-lavender light, each curved like a sabre blade, that billow up out of the book and curl round behind her, all joined to the book. It is plainly a drawing coming to life.
pose: On two legs, she steps forward to the left, turned three-quarters, weight on her bent front leg, the open sketchbook held out to the left at arm's length in her left hand, her right hand sweeping the quill across the page, her head up, her robe and her dark hair billowing in the wind of the magic.
